ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicists suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega=8.56 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L=1.00 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $M=9.50 \mathrm{~kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge of the door is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break at where the bending moment is largest. (Answer in metres.)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the door is simplified as a horizontal thin rod, the left end is a hinge/axis of rotation, beside it is marked angular velocity ω; an external force F upward vertically is applied at the right end; the distance from the hinge to a certain cross section on the rod is marked as x. Then reason: Treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length L and mass M, with linear density λ = M/L. The whole door rotates around the hinge, and the rotational equation about the hinge is F L = I_h α. The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about an endpoint is I_h = (1/3) M L^2, so F L = (1/3) M L^2 α, therefore F = (1/3) M L α. Make a cross section at a distance x from the hinge, and take the right-side rod segment x <= r <= L for force analysis. According to d'Alembert's method, on the right-side rod segment there is a tangential inertial load density λ α r. The bending moment at the cross section equals the moment of the endpoint force F minus the moment of the distributed inertial load: B(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λ α r(r - x) dr. Substitute F = (1/3) M L α and λ = M/L, and simplifying gives B(x) = M α x(L^2 - x^2)/(6L). The door is most likely to break at the place where the bending moment is greatest, therefore set the derivative to zero: dB/dx = M α/(6L) · (L^2 - 3x^2) = 0, so L^2 - 3x^2 = 0, obtaining x = L/sqrt(3). In the problem L = 1.00 m, therefore x = 1/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)/3 m ≈ 0.577 m.

raw_record.question_text:
During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicist's suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega=8.56\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L=1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ and mass $M=9.50\ \mathrm{kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break where the bending moment is largest. Answer in metres.

method.method_draft: Use a free-body diagram of the rod segment to the right of an arbitrary cut at distance x from the hinge. From the whole-door rotational equation, the applied end force satisfies F L=I_h alpha=(1/3) M L^2 alpha, so F=(1/3)M L alpha. For the segment x<=r<=L, include the D'Alembert tangential inertial load density lambda alpha r, where lambda=M/L. The bending moment at the cut is the end-force moment minus the moment of this distributed inertial load: B(x)=F(L-x)-int_x^L lambda alpha r(r-x) dr. This simplifies to B(x)=M alpha x(L^2-x^2)/(6L). Maximize by setting dB/dx=0, giving L^2-3x^2=0, so x=L/sqrt(3)=sqrt(3)/3 m for L=1.00 m.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中门被简化为一根水平细杆，左端是铰链/转轴，旁边标有角速度 ω；右端施加竖直向上的外力 F；从铰链到杆上某一截面的距离标为 x。

再推理：把门看成长度 L、质量 M 的均匀细杆，线密度为 λ = M/L。整扇门绕铰链转动，关于铰链的转动方程为 F L = I_h α。均匀细杆绕端点的转动惯量为 I_h = (1/3) M L^2，所以 F L = (1/3) M L^2 α，因此 F = (1/3) M L α。

在距离铰链 x 处作截面，取右侧杆段 x <= r <= L 作受力分析。按照达朗贝尔方法，右侧杆段上有切向惯性载荷密度 λ α r。截面处弯矩等于端点力 F 的力矩减去分布惯性载荷的力矩：B(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λ α r(r - x) dr。

代入 F = (1/3) M L α 和 λ = M/L，化简得到 B(x) = M α x(L^2 - x^2)/(6L)。门最可能在弯矩最大的地方断裂，因此令导数为零：dB/dx = M α/(6L) · (L^2 - 3x^2) = 0，所以 L^2 - 3x^2 = 0，得到 x = L/sqrt(3)。题中 L = 1.00 m，因此 x = 1/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)/3 m ≈ 0.577 m。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer sqrt(3)/3 m is exactly the same value as the standard answer \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\), with the correct unit in metres.

method.method_draft: Use the shear-force criterion instead of first writing the full moment curve. Convert the angular acceleration into an equivalent tangential distributed inertia load w(r)=lambda alpha r along the rod, opposing the applied force. Determine the tip force from the whole rod: F=I_h alpha/L=(1/3)M L alpha. For a cut at x, the internal shear associated with the outer piece is V(x)=F-int_x^L w(r) dr. A local extremum of bending moment occurs where the shear is zero. Thus set F=int_x^L (M/L) alpha r dr=(M alpha/(2L))(L^2-x^2). Substituting F=(1/3)M L alpha gives x^2=L^2/3, hence x=L/sqrt(3)=sqrt(3)/3 m. Boundary moments vanish at the hinge cut and free end in this reduced model, so this interior extremum is the maximum.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图显示一根水平细杆表示门，左端为铰链/转轴，门绕左端以角速度 omega 转动；右端受到向上的外力 F；距离铰链为 x 的位置被标出，用来表示可能断裂的位置。

推理：按指定的剪力判据处理。把门看作长度 L、质量 M 的均匀细杆，线密度 lambda = M/L。角加速度为 alpha 时，距铰链 r 处的切向惯性分布载荷为 w(r) = lambda alpha r = (M/L) alpha r，方向与外力造成的切向加速度相反。

先由整根杆关于铰链的转动方程确定端力 F：F L = I_h alpha，其中端点铰链处的转动惯量 I_h = (1/3) M L^2，所以 F = I_h alpha / L = (1/3) M L alpha。

在距铰链 x 处切开，考虑外侧区段 x 到 L。该截面的内剪力为 V(x) = F - integral_x^L w(r) dr。弯矩的局部极值出现在剪力为零的位置，因此令 F = integral_x^L (M/L) alpha r dr = (M alpha/(2L))(L^2 - x^2)。

代入 F = (1/3) M L alpha，得到 (1/3) M L alpha = (M alpha/(2L))(L^2 - x^2)。消去 M 和 alpha：L/3 = (L^2 - x^2)/(2L)，所以 2L^2/3 = L^2 - x^2，得到 x^2 = L^2/3。因此 x = L/sqrt(3)。给定 L = 1.00 m，所以 x = 1/sqrt(3) m = sqrt(3)/3 m，约为 0.577 m。边界处弯矩在该简化模型中为零，因此这个内部极值为最大弯矩位置。

代入 F = (1/3) M L alpha，得到 (1/3) M L alpha = (M alpha/(2L))(L^2 - x^2)。消去 M 和 alpha：L/3 = (L^2 - x^2)/(2L)，所以 2L^2/3 = L^2 - x^2，得到 x^2 = L^2/3。因此 x = L/sqrt(3)。给定 L = 1.00 m，所以 x = 1/sqrt(3) m = sqrt(3)/3 m，约为 0.577 m。边界处弯矩在该简化模型中为零，因此这个内部极值为最大弯矩位置。

raw_record.original_question:
During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicist's suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega=8.56\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L=1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ and mass $M=9.50\ \mathrm{kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break where the bending moment is largest. Answer in metres.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, the door is simplified as a horizontal thin rod, the left end is a hinge/axis of rotation, beside it is marked angular velocity ω; an external force F upward vertically is applied at the right end; the distance from the hinge to a certain cross section on the rod is marked as x.

Then reason: Treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length L and mass M, with linear density λ = M/L. The whole door rotates around the hinge, and the rotational equation about the hinge is F L = I_h α. The moment of inertia of a uniform thin rod about an endpoint is I_h = (1/3) M L^2, so F L = (1/3) M L^2 α, therefore F = (1/3) M L α.

Make a cross section at a distance x from the hinge, and take the right-side rod segment x <= r <= L for force analysis. According to d'Alembert's method, on the right-side rod segment there is a tangential inertial load density λ α r. The bending moment at the cross section equals the moment of the endpoint force F minus the moment of the distributed inertial load: B(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λ α r(r - x) dr.

Substitute F = (1/3) M L α and λ = M/L, and simplifying gives B(x) = M α x(L^2 - x^2)/(6L). The door is most likely to break at the place where the bending moment is greatest, therefore set the derivative to zero: dB/dx = M α/(6L) · (L^2 - 3x^2) = 0, so L^2 - 3x^2 = 0, obtaining x = L/sqrt(3). In the problem L = 1.00 m, therefore x = 1/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3)/3 m ≈ 0.577 m.
